entry: Cacheable, CachePut and CacheEvict with subscriber Context

questions.history: Call lookup("k") first under t1, then under t2 with the same key. Inspect cache.get("k").get().
questions.prediction: The PR reports [none] twice before. On the landing expect [t1] twice, a stored list [t1], and one source subscription.
questions.basis: The first caller supplies the value on a miss. Both method arguments identify the same cache entry even though the second subscriber has a different context.
questions.refutation: The first result loses t1, the hit observes t2, or the two calls run the producer twice.

questions.history: Use a fresh cache and an otherwise equivalent @Cacheable `Mono<String>` based on Mono.deferContextual. Make the same miss and hit.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should emit t1 on the miss and on the repeated key.
questions.basis: The single-value reactive path supplies a control for the Flux sharing introduced by the cache collector. The upstream regression includes both publisher types.
questions.refutation: The Mono loses its context on a miss or changes value on a hit.

questions.history: On fresh state, call a Flux-returning @CachePut("first") for "k" under t1; then call a Flux-returning @CacheEvict("first") for "k" under t2. Both sources emit "tenant" as above.
questions.prediction: On the landing expect [t1] and cache value [t1] after put, then [t2] and an absent key after eviction.
questions.basis: Put stores a completed result, eviction removes it. Both operations expose their own caller’s context through the returned stream.
questions.refutation: The cache changes correctly but either Flux emits none, or the Flux has the right value and the cache transition fails.

questions.history: Hold "k" fixed. Save the cacheable Flux before attaching any context; first subscribe under t1. Evict "k" explicitly through Cache.evict("k"), obtain a new lookup("k") Flux and subscribe under t2.
questions.prediction: The landing should deliver [t1] followed by [t2], subscribe to the producer twice, and end with cache value [t2].
questions.basis: Each call is a confirmed miss; subscription determines the Reactor Context. Emptying the entry prevents an earlier stored value from answering for the second context.
questions.refutation: A miss reads the assembly-time default or reuses t1 after eviction.
